newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spot mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spot mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Tuesday on a technical correction after sharp gains on Monday, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell sharply to 10.00 percent from 15.55 percent.
Turnover fell to 5.57 million lots from 11.65 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Big institutions reduced their trading today after borrowing huge amounts of money on Monday to speculate on the surging domestic A share market, traders said.

"The rates are likely to move in a narrow range for the rest of this week, with institutions having a lot of money in hand and the repo rates at appropriate levels after today's falls," one trader said.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed in slow trading on Tuesday and traders said market sentiment was poor, with the market having fallen for weeks. Volume of the eight-contract market fell to 773,433 lots from 1.18 million.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell to 120.00 yuan from 120.13 yuan.
